title: Ulyana and the House
premise: Zephyrine Nystrom returns to the family house to bury his twin sister Ulyana, only to discover the coffin holds a stranger wearing her face. The house itself begins keeping time wrong: every mirror lags one second behind reality, and in that stolen second Zephyrine glimpses Ulyana, alive, mouthing an old harvest song their grandmother taught them. As the harvest moon waxes, he learns the house has been trading Nystrom children for generations, and that the 'wrong sibling' buried was the house's first attempt to replace him. To free Ulyana from the reflection-world before the moon rises full, Zephyrine must learn the song's forbidden last verse — but singing it aloud binds the singer to the house forever. In the end he sings it silently, offering himself as the house's keeper instead of its sacrifice; Ulyana steps out of the glass, and Zephyrine remains as the house's living memory, lights on, doors counted, until she comes home again.
about_author: Lena Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales in rural Scandinavia, where she collected the funeral songs and household superstitions that haunt her fiction. She writes at night, in houses other people have left.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sister
chapters.summary: Zephyrine arrives at the Nystrom house for the viewing and recognizes immediately that the body in the coffin is not Ulyana. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as the undertaker avoids his questions and the house seems to lean in and listen.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Zephyrine stays the night out of stubbornness, following childhood rituals: every lamp lit, every door counted twice. He finds Ulyana's journal hidden in the stairwell. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the comfort of ritual turning sinister as the count comes out wrong — thirteen doors in a nine-door house.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin lagging. Zephyrine tests them with a dropped cup, watching it fall a heartbeat after it lands. In the delay, a figure moves in the glass that isn't him. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: rational denial cracking into terror.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Remember
chapters.summary: Zephyrine visits elderly neighbor Marta Voss, who reveals the Nystroms always buried 'a stranger' once a generation, and that the harvest song was never meant to be finished. POV: Zephyrine with Marta's recounted memories. Emotional beat: the horror of inheritance — this is family tradition, not haunting.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Journal
chapters.summary: Reading the journal, Zephyrine learns Ulyana discovered the mirror-lag months ago and had been learning the song's last verse deliberately, believing she could trade herself willingly to save him. POV: interwoven journal entries and Zephyrine's reactions. Emotional beat: guilt — she died, or vanished, protecting him.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: He unseals grandmother Signe's locked room and finds sheet music missing its final page, torn away, plus photographs of Nystrom twins going back two centuries — always twins, always one lost. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: awe and violation; the room is warm, as if recently left.

chapters.title: Reflections That Watch Back
chapters.summary: The lag widens to three seconds. Zephyrine sees Ulyana clearly now, mouthing words, pointing behind him. The reflections of the house show rooms that don't exist. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: desperate hope — she's alive somewhere — tangled with fear of what's pointing at his back.

chapters.title: Marta's Warning
chapters.summary: Marta begs him to leave before the moon fills, telling of a man in 1961 who sang along to the song and became part of the house — she shows Zephyrine the man's face, still faintly visible in her own old mirror. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the temptation to flee versus the impossibility of abandoning Ulyana.

chapters.title: Thirteen Doors
chapters.summary: The extra doors are real now, appearing in walls Zephyrine knows by heart. Behind one he hears humming — the song, sung slightly ahead of him, correcting his memory. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: disorientation; the house is rehearsing him.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Following the humming, Zephyrine enters a mirrored corridor and speaks to Ulyana through the glass for the first time. She can hear him but answers only in fragments of verse. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: reunion and heartbreak — touching the glass, both palms aligned, seconds apart.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Half-moon. The house grows hungry: food spoils overnight, clocks all read different hours, and Zephyrine catches himself humming the song without deciding to. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: erosion of self — the house is teaching him whether he consents or not.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Coffin
chapters.summary: Zephyrine exhumes the grave and finds the stranger's corpse aging rapidly into a likeness of himself. Clutched in its hand: the torn final page of the sheet music, mostly illegible. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: revulsion and grim resolve — the house already made its replacement for him once.

chapters.title: Signe's Confession
chapters.summary: In a hidden letter, grandmother Signe admits she completed the verse once, as a girl, and traded her own twin to escape; the house has held the debt open ever since. POV: Zephyrine reading. Emotional beat: fury at the dead, and the terrible knowledge that the last verse exists inside someone still living — Marta.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Marta confesses she was Signe's accomplice and carries the verse in memory but refuses to speak it, having watched what it did to Signe. She offers Zephyrine an alternative: leave tonight, let the house keep Ulyana, live. POV: dual — Marta's account framed by Zephyrine's silence. Emotional beat: moral weight; survival offered as the cruelest gift.

chapters.title: Waxing
chapters.summary: Three nights from full. The lag reverses — mirrors now show events before they happen, including Zephyrine standing at the front door, singing. He refuses to make the vision true. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: defiance against fate, and the first hint the house fears him.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Zephyrine stops fighting the rituals and performs them perfectly, and the house responds: doors lead where he intends, the corridor of glass opens fully. He realizes belonging is the mechanism — the house takes those who belong. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: eerie communion; he understands the house because he is like it.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Through the glass, Ulyana teaches him the verse note by note while he mouths it silently, hands pressed together through the mirror. Each correct note makes the lag shrink. POV: alternating Zephyrine and Ulyana's muffled perspective. Emotional beat: tenderness under extremity — siblings relearning each other across a boundary of silvered glass.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Marta dies peacefully in her sleep, and with her last breath on the phone hums the final phrase — completing what Zephyrine lacked. The house shudders; every mirror goes dark. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief braided with dread — he has everything he needs, and no way back from using it.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Full moonrise. The house pulls Zephyrine toward the great hall mirror, the vision from the waxing night trying to fulfill itself. He walks in willingly but on his own terms, silent-verse ready, refusing the song's trap. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into agency.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Inside the reflection-world, Zephyrine sings the verse soundlessly, offering himself not as sacrifice but as keeper — rewriting the contract's meaning. The house accepts; Ulyana is expelled through the glass into the living world. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: climax — self-gift without self-destruction, love as terms negotiated.

chapters.title: Keeper of the House
chapters.summary: Ulyana wakes on the hallway floor; Zephyrine is gone from the mirrors but present everywhere else — in the lamps that stay lit, the doors that count themselves. She buries the stranger properly and chooses to stay. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: mourning fused with devotion; belonging claimed rather than imposed.

chapters.title: Coda: Lights On
chapters.summary: Years later, Ulyana keeps the rituals, and each harvest moon the mirrors lag exactly one second — long enough for brother and sister to press palms to the glass. The last verse is never sung aloud again. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — memory and inheritance reconciled, belonging made a choice renewed yearly.
